reasoning: The test uses Playwright's APIRequestContext (the 'request' fixture) to make POST API calls like `request.post('/api/people/create', ...)` and `request.post('/api/faces/assign', ...)`. The application has CSRF protection enabled via `security.py`'s `@app.before_request protect_unsafe_request`, which blocks all non-safe HTTP methods (POST, PUT, DELETE) unless a valid `X-CSRF-Token` header or `csrf_token` form field is present. The browser's `static/security.js` intercepts `window.fetch()` and automatically injects the `X-CSRF-Token` header from `window.APP_CONFIG.csrfToken`, but Playwright's `APIRequestContext` bypasses the browser entirely and does not include any CSRF token. This causes every API POST to return 403 instead of 201. The face_assignment test suite (`face-assignment.spec.ts`) correctly avoids this by using `page.evaluate()` with `fetch()` for all API calls, which routes through `security.js`'s interceptor. The failure is 100% reproducible across all 3 test runs (identical error at the same line). This is not an application regression (CSRF protection is working as designed) and not an environment issue (the app is correctly configured).
suggestedAction: Rewrite createPersonViaApi and assignFaceToPersonViaApi to accept Page instead of APIRequestContext and use page.evaluate() with fetch() (following the pattern in face-assignment.spec.ts). Replace all inline request.post(...) cleanup calls with page.evaluate()-based fetch calls. Remove the APIRequestContext import and the request fixture from test function signatures.
